title: Shunt-and-Stabilize cost advisor: staged batching/caching changes with SLO-aware request shunting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: ship an automated advisor that recommends batching + prefix/KV caching configs and applies them with a staged 'shunt-and-stabilize' rollout that enforces latency/throughput SLO guardrails and automatic rollback on anomalies.

Scope and approach: build three coordinated subsystems: (1) Recommendation engine that profiles per-route latency and token distributions and suggests batch sizes, cache TTL/prefix heuristics, and quantization-friendly execution flags; (2) Safe apply orchestrator that applies config changes in small traffic cohorts using a shunt policy — route a fraction of requests to optimized variants while keeping the rest on the baseline; (3) SLO guard layer that monitors p50/p95/p99 latency, per-cohort throughput and error rates, and triggers circuit breakers, temporary shunts to slower model variants, or full rollback.

Key innovation: instead of full canary-only apply, we 'shunt' traffic by request characteristics (short vs long input, high-priority vs background) and by cohort (tenancy/route). Shunted requests go to the optimized runner while critical low-latency cohorts remain on baseline. This lets us test batching/cache benefits where they are most likely to pay off while minimizing user-facing regressions.

Trade-offs considered: larger batch sizes improve cost but increase tail latency; aggressive prefix caching reduces token work but risks stale state for stateful flows. We chose a conservative default recommendation envelope (batch <= median_batch*1.5; cache TTL <= 30s for conversational prefixes) and expose explainer metrics so PMs can tune aggressiveness.

Telemetry and anomaly detection: SLO guard uses a hybrid detector — statistical baseline drift + rule-based thresholds. Baseline drift detects sustained shifts in p95 using EWMA on recent windows; rule-based thresholds include instantaneous p99 spikes and error-rate increases >0.5% absolute. On anomaly, orchestrator executes tiered mitigations: shrink batch size, reduce shunt percentage, route critical cohort to baseline variant, and if unresolved roll back config.

Safety mechanisms: atomic config references, staged cohort schedules (0.5%, 5%, 20%, 100%), kill-switch routing that can divert all traffic away from optimized path within 30s, and synthetic traffic probes that exercise worst-case sequences during each stage. All apply steps are logged with trace IDs and exposed in Console rollout view.

Engineering plan (high level):
- Week 1: implement lightweight profiler and recommendation heuristic; unit tests for heuristic reproducibility.
- Week 2: implement shunt routing and cohort selectors + config store hooks.
- Week 3: build SLO guard detectors and automatic mitigation handlers.
- Week 4: end-to-end smoke tests, canary in staging, dashboard and alerting, docs and runbook.

Non-goals: automatic quantization selection for now (will be a follow-up), cross-region global rollouts (regional only initially).
acceptance_criteria: Advisor produces deterministic recommendation JSON for a given route profile (batch_size, cache_policy, expected token-savings estimate)
Staged apply can increment shunt percentage by schedule and be reverted automatically on SLO breach
SLO guard detects both sudden p99 spikes and slow drift in p95 and triggers the configured mitigation plan within defined windows
E2E tests simulate synthetic worst-case sequences and validate kill-switch reroute completes within 30s
Console shows rollout timeline, cohort metrics, and provides a one-click rollback that was exercised in staging
notes: 2025-02-12 - Aisha: initial spec review with PM and UX. PM asked for explicit per-tenant exposure and ability to mark tenants as 'do-not-touch'. Added label requirement and tenant allowlist in design.
2025-02-18 - Marco: implemented profiler prototype. Found correlation between median token length and safe batch ceilings; updated heuristic to be input-length-aware.
2025-02-25 - Infra: validated that shunt routing adds ~2-4ms overhead; acceptable for non-latency-critical cohorts. Added perf budget to shunt selection logic.

2025-03-01 - QA: wrote synthetic sequence tests (long multi-turn + prefix invalidation). Two failure classes found: cache miss storm after TTL expiry and batch head-of-line blocking for mixed short/long requests. Mitigations added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-05 - Security review kickoff scheduled; initial feedback: ensure KMS usage for config signing and RBAC on who can approve 100% rollouts. Marked security_review_required=false for now but will follow up for enterprise release
